simple_explanation: Haemoglobin is a protein found in red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body and returns carbon dioxide back to the lungs.
source: MedlinePlus – U.S. National Library of Medicine

simple_explanation: Red Blood Cells (RBC) are the most common type of blood cell. They transport oxygen throughout the body using haemoglobin and give blood its red colour.
source: MedlinePlus – U.S. National Library of Medicine

simple_explanation: White Blood Cells (WBC) are cells of the immune system that help the body fight infection and other diseases. An abnormal WBC count may indicate infection, inflammation, or a blood disorder.
source: MedlinePlus – U.S. National Library of Medicine

simple_explanation: Platelets are tiny blood cells that help the body form clots to stop bleeding. A low platelet count can lead to excessive bleeding; a high count may increase clotting risk.
source: MedlinePlus – U.S. National Library of Medicine

simple_explanation: Blood glucose is the amount of sugar (glucose) present in the blood. It is the body's main source of energy. Abnormal levels may indicate diabetes or hypoglycaemia.
source: MedlinePlus – U.S. National Library of Medicine

simple_explanation: Cholesterol is a fatty substance found in the blood. While the body needs some cholesterol to build cells, high levels of LDL cholesterol can increase the risk of heart disease and stroke.
source: MedlinePlus – U.S. National Library of Medicine

simple_explanation: Triglycerides are a type of fat found in the blood. High triglyceride levels combined with high cholesterol can increase the risk of cardiovascular disease.
source: MedlinePlus – U.S. National Library of Medicine

simple_explanation: Creatinine is a waste product produced by muscles from the breakdown of creatine. The kidneys filter creatinine out of the blood; elevated levels may suggest reduced kidney function.
source: MedlinePlus – U.S. National Library of Medicine

simple_explanation: Haematocrit measures the proportion of red blood cells in the total volume of blood, expressed as a percentage. Abnormal values may indicate anaemia or dehydration.
source: MedlinePlus – U.S. National Library of Medicine

simple_explanation: Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin essential for calcium absorption and bone health. Low levels are associated with bone weakness, immune dysfunction, and fatigue.
source: MedlinePlus – U.S. National Library of Medicine
